text:
nina_csm: Heads-up from the weekly health check: Aurora dedicated pool hit a big surge overnight. Dropping quick summary and action items. cc @tariq_infra @lucy_ops @ben_se @eli_fin

tariq_infra: Morning. Raw numbers 00:00-06:00 UTC: reserved_hours=1000h/month, used_last_7d=764h (76%), avg_saturation=74%, peak_saturation=99% (00:47 UTC), avg_queue_depth=9, max_queue_depth=45. Spike correlates with nightly benchmark+eval sweep. Dashboard: https://redwood-ops.internal/dashboards/aurora/pool

lucy_ops: Oof max depth 45. That will cause p99 latency >2s based on our tail curves. Did deploy-bot catch any auto-throttle events?

deploy-bot: ALERT: pool aurora-dedicated queue_depth > 40 at 2100112389 (autoscaler throttled lower-priority jobs) :warning:

ben_se: Checked job attribution: top GPU consumers were aurora-evals (60%), aurora-batch (14%), partner-analytics (7%). Aurora team rolled new eval matrix last night to stress test a quantized variant.

eli_fin: FYI finance flagged this morning 50 spike on their weekly bill. Renewal review scheduled in 6 weeks; they're sensitive to surprises.

nina_csm: Proposed immediate steps: 1) ask Aurora to shift non-critical evals to late-night maintenance window (03:00-06:00 UTC) 2) apply per-tenant concurrency caps for eval jobs 3) enable temporary burst pool (500 hours) while we model reserve vs burst economics.

tariq_infra: I can push a per-tenant concurrency patch and a priority class so partner-analytics stays below evaluation jobs. Patch snippet: ```yaml
pool: aurora-dedicated
priority_classes: [realtime, eval, background]
concurrency_caps:
  eval: 10
  background: 2
burst_pool_hours: 500
```
Rolling to canary now.

lucy_ops: Ops plan: - canary the cap (owner: tariq_infra) - enable burst pool in test (owner: ben_se) - run cost estimate for finance (owner: eli_fin) - coordinate maintenance window with customer (owner: nina_csm). Target <36h.

ben_se: Canary sim results: with cap=10 and burst=500, projected max_queue_depth falls to 12, p99 latency to ~0.65s. Cost delta for week ~+8% if burst used at peak. If we instead bump reserved commit by 15% cost would be +12% monthly but smoother.

eli_fin: Collating numbers for comparison (burst vs reserve). Will share a short table ahead of the renewal workshop.

nina_csm: Can we get a brief customer note by EOD explaining short-term burst + proposal to evaluate reserving more capacity for next quarter? They'd rather know the options in writing.

tariq_infra: Canary promoted to prod at 2100112780. Immediate telemetry: queue_depth avg 4, max 13 over the following hour. Watching for rebound.

ben_se: Uploaded runbook + config diff to the repo: https://redwood-share/internal/aurora/runbooks/dedicated-capacity-mitigation.md

lucy_ops: I'll run the 72h stabilization check and post results next Wed. If we see repeated spikes tied to scheduled evals, recommend moving heavy eval jobs to a weekly offload on dedicated batch infra.

nina_csm: Next steps recap: - tariq_infra: confirm 24h stability + post p99 metrics - ben_se: finalize burst provisioning playbook - eli_fin: deliver cost comparison - nina_csm: draft customer-facing summary + propose 30-min renewal prep slot.

eli_fin: Sending preliminary finance note now. Customer asked for a quick estimate for a 15% reserved uplift vs bursts; I'll include both numbers.

nina_csm: Thanks team 60 keep this thread updated with short status posts. We'll escalate to the account exec if stabilization isn't achieved within 48h. :thumbsup:
